worked_example.problem: How does an {p} reproduce naturally without seeds?
steps: An Irish potato is a stem tuber: a swollen underground stem full of stored food.
Its buds (eyes) grow into new shoots, using the stored food, and each forms a new plant.
worked_example.answer: By stem tubers: the buds (eyes) grow into new plants.

cards.idea: Vegetative propagation grows new plants from stems, roots or leaves, not from seeds.
example: A banana sucker becomes a new banana plant.
A ginger rhizome grows new shoots.

cards.idea: Underground storage organs feed the new plant: bulbs, corms, rhizomes, tubers.
example: Irish potato: stem tuber. Sweet potato: root tuber.

cards.idea: Some plants make new plants from their leaves or from runners.
example: Bryophyllum: plantlets on the leaf edges.
Some grasses: runners along the ground.

pick.q: Which plant forms new plantlets on the edges of its leaves?
e: Mango grows from seeds or grafts.
pick.y: Bryophyllum has buds on its leaf edges.

pick.q: Banana and plantain reproduce naturally by …
e: Cultivated bananas have no good seeds.
Their leaves do not make plantlets.
pick.y: Suckers grow from the base of the stem.

pick.q: Spear grass is hard to get rid of because it spreads by …
pick.y: Pieces of rhizome left in the soil grow again.

questions.prompt: Match each plant to the organ it uses for natural vegetative propagation.

e: A root tuber is a swollen root, like sweet potato.
A bulb has fleshy leaves, like onion.
pick.y: It is a swollen stem with buds (eyes).

e: Sweet potato is a swollen root.
A corm is a short swollen stem.
A rhizome is a horizontal stem.

pick.q: Why do most vegetative organs contain stored food?
pick.r: to feed the new plant until it can make its own food
e: That is the job of petals.
pick.y: Stored food feeds the young shoots.
